items.title: Trump’s attempt to rename AI is looking awfully artificial
items.description:
President Donald Trump has a knack for turning words against his enemies. items.content: President Donald Trump has a knack for turning words against his enemies. His first successful presidential run was built on monikers like “Little Marco” and “Crooked Hillary”; he changed “fake news” from a phrase describing scammy media outlets to a derogatory term for the press at large. Over the past few weeks, he’s clearly decided he can work the same magic to promote artificial intelligence — branding a technology he wants to accelerate “super”, while turning “artificial” into his latest go-to pejorative and declaring resisters “THE ENEMY.” Some of the biggest names in AI are going along with him. But he’s picked a tough linguistic battle, and it may not pan out the way he hopes.A longtime AI booster, Trump has gone into pro-robot overdrive since an industry conversation over “pacing” frontier development last month. His current position is that AI safety risks are overblown and US companies need to speed up development, including by building more data centers, which he insists contrary to polling data will be “very popular.” On top of discouraging industry self-regulation, he’s decided AI needs a rebrand by fiat. Trump declared in a rambling United Nations speech last month that “the use of the word artificial makes intelligence fake” and promised to rename the technology “super intelligence.” He then followed through with an executive order last week, forbidding the use of “AI” wherever possible.Image: Truth SocialChanges have been swift. The US Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI), already a rebrand of the AI Safety Institute, has been renamed the Center for Advancing Innovation and Standards for Super Intelligence (CAISSI). Justice Department press releases have been modified to include the phrase, trumpeting that a man who flooded streaming platforms with AI-generated songs between 2017 and 2024 committed “Super Intelligence-Assisted Music Streaming Fraud.” On Thursday, Trump declared that “The White House considers anyone that uses the term, ‘Artificial Intelligence,’ as opposed to the highly accepted new and more accurate term, ‘Super Intelligence,’ THE ENEMY!”The same tech company figures who rushed to donate millions to Trump after his election have quickly signed on. Trump’s “First Buddy” Elon Musk has promised to rename SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI, while Jeff Bezos declared he likes it because “artificial is not a very flattering thing.” Jensen Huang, whom Trump called live on stage last month to rant that “robots will not be taking over,” has likewise adopted the term. Sam Altman praised it too, though he said OpenAI won’t be changing its name.As Trump tries to make SI happen, “artificial” is creeping into his vocabulary in the manner of earlier terms like “hoax” and “fake.” He recently announced that his long-favored epithet “fake news media” would be retired in favor of calling the press “artificial media,” and in an October 5th campaign rally (shortly before musing that Iran could “take out” Los Angeles and San Diego) he declared that concerns about war driving up prices were “just artificial.”As publicly happy as some AI industry figures have seemed with “SI”, Trump is functionally demanding a major industry rewrite its terminology. “Superintelligence” (one word) long predates Trump’s affection for “super”; it was popularized in an eponymous 2014 book by Nick Bostrom. But the term denotes highly advanced artificial intelligence that could surpass human thought, not the category of AI — an already nebulous term — as a whole. It’s one of several industry buzzwords (alongside artificial general intelligence and “useful general intelligence”) meant to define what comes after the current iteration of the tech.Trump is functionally demanding a major industry rewrite its terminologyTrump adopting “super intelligence” might seem good for companies that had already hitched their wagon to superintelligence, including Meta and Microsoft. And as public opinion turns against AI, some in the industry may desire a rebrand. But forcing immediate adoption of SI also undercuts companies’ ability to promote big, new, flashy AI products as “superintelligent”, instead applying the term to everything from a future machine god to years-old music-slop generation tools. The field is even taking a downgrade with that additional corny space in the middle, since Trump’s attempts at earnestly good names have never really measured up to his insults.Meanwhile, Trump will have to convince the other branches of government to get on board with the term. He can’t bar Congress from using “artificial intelligence,” and it appears in existing laws like Trump’s signature Take It Down Act, which administration agencies will need to cite when arguing in court. As appetite for more AI regulation grows, congressional Republicans will have to decide whether to appease Trump by adopting a name many people find unintuitive, freighted with the baggage of Trump’s fairly unpopular pro-industry, anti-regulatory stance.And to make things even more confusing, pro-regulation figures like Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-VT) were already using the earlier definition of superintelligence in efforts to restrict powerful AI — Sanders cosponsored a bill called the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act in early September.Trump loves naming things, but his linguistic victories typically work when they’re catchy: either simple nicknames or distinctively funny turns of phrase. (Many people are saying!) “Super intelligence,” by contrast, simply comes off as a euphemism. A lot of Americans have tangible gripes with the industry, particularly around data centers, and insisting the tech is “super” does nothing to assuage these concerns. If anything, Trump’s escalating attempts to strong-arm people into a supposedly nicer term for AI makes him — and the industry itself — look awfully weak.

items.titleZh: 特朗普试图给AI改名，此举显得极为人工。
items.descriptionZh:
特朗普正试图发动一场AI命名战。文章开篇回顾了他擅长用语言打击对手的历史：从“Little Marco”“Crooked Hillary”，到把“fake news”从描述不良媒体变成对整个新闻界的贬称。如今，他想把同样手法用在AI上：把他希望加速发展的技术称为“super”，把“artificial”变成新的贬义词，并把抵制者称为“THE ENEMY”。一些AI界最重要的人物正在跟随他。

背景是，特朗普长期支持AI。上个月，在业界围绕是否要“pacing”（控制节奏）前沿AI开发的讨论之后，他进入了亲机器人的“超速”状态。他现在的立场是：AI安全风险被夸大，美国公司需要加快开发，包括建设更多数据中心；他坚称数据中心会“非常受欢迎”，尽管民调数据相反。除了反对行业自我监管，他还决定用行政力量给AI改名。上个月，他在联合国讲话中宣称“artificial”这个词让智能显得虚假，并承诺把这项技术改名为“super intelligence”。上周，他签署行政令，禁止在可能的情况下使用“AI”。

改名行动迅速展开。美国AI标准与创新中心（CAISI，本身已是AI安全研究所的改名）又被改名为“超级智能推进创新与标准中心”（CAISSI）。司法部新闻稿也被修改，宣称一名在2017至2024年间向流媒体平台大量发布AI生成歌曲的男子犯下了“Super Intelligence-Assisted Music Streaming Fraud”。周四，特朗普宣布：“白宫认为，任何使用‘Artificial Intelligence’而不是更准确的新词‘Super Intelligence’的人，都是THE ENEMY！”

科技界一些大佬迅速跟进。特朗普的“第一伙伴”马斯克承诺把SpaceXAI改名为SpaceXSI；贝索斯表示喜欢这个说法，因为“artificial听起来不太好”；黄仁勋也采用了这个词——上个月特朗普曾在舞台上现场连线他，并声称“机器人不会接管”；Sam Altman也称赞这一命名，但表示OpenAI不会改名。

与此同时，特朗普正把“artificial”变成类似“hoax”“fake”的贬义词。他宣布不再使用长期偏好的“fake news media”，而是改称媒体为“artificial media”；在10月5日竞选集会上，他还称对战争推高物价的担忧“just artificial”。

但这场语言战并不容易赢。学界早已使用一个词的“superintelligence”，该词由Nick Bostrom在2014年同名书中普及，指的是可能超越人类思维的高度先进AI，而不是AI这个整体类别。它和AGI、“useful general intelligence”一样，是定义当前技术之后阶段的行业热词。特朗普强推“Super Intelligence”（两个词）会造成术语混乱。对Meta、微软等已押注超级智能的公司来说，这看似有利；在公众对AI反感上升时，一些公司也可能想要重塑品牌。但强制立即采用SI，会削弱企业把重大新AI产品宣传为“超级智能”的能力，因为这个标签会被套到从未来机器神到多年前音乐垃圾生成工具的一切东西上。中间多出的空格，还让这个领域显得掉价、土气。特朗普认真取的好名字，通常比不上他的贬称。

政治和法律上也有障碍。特朗普无法禁止国会使用“artificial intelligence”，这个词已出现在现有法律中，例如他标志性的《Take It Down Act》，行政机构在法庭上仍需引用。随着AI监管呼声增长，国会共和党人必须决定是否迎合特朗普，采用一个许多人觉得不直观、且背负其不受欢迎的亲产业、反监管立场的名字。更混乱的是，支持监管的参议员Bernie Sanders等人早已使用“superintelligence”的旧定义来推动限制强大AI，并在9月初共同提出《Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act》。

结论是，特朗普热爱命名，但他的语言胜利通常靠朗朗上口：简单绰号或独特搞笑的措辞。相比之下，“Super Intelligence”更像一种委婉语。许多美国人对AI产业有具体不满，尤其是数据中心；坚称这项技术“super”，并不能缓解这些担忧。若继续强推，反而会让他和AI行业显得虚弱。原文没有涉及具体技术原理、芯片性能或对比数据；其核心是AI命名、监管与产业政治。

items.title: Kioxia unveils E1.L SSDs for hyperscalers with up to 122.88TB capacity
items.description: Kioxia's LD4-series SSDs can store up to 122.88TB of data in a compact form-factor, but its performance remains a mystery.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Kioxia introduced its LD4-series solid-state drives (SSDs) in an E1.L form factor with capacities up to 122.88TB designed for high-density storage deployments in hyperscale data centers on Friday. The new drives use proven BiCS8 3D QLC NAND and are aimed at read-intensive workloads like AI data repositories and object storage, according to the manufacturer.Tom's Hardware Premium Roadmaps (Image credit: Future)Leading-edge foundry roadmapsNvidia Enterprise GPU and CPU roadmapAMD's Enterprise GPU and CPU roadmapIntel's roadmaps examined — 14A, Nova Lake, Diamond Rapids & AI accelerator pushCo-Packaged Optics (CPO) foundry roadmapsKioxia's LD4-series SSDs rely on the company's proprietary platform complying with the NVMe 2.0e specification and featuring a single-port configuration along with select requirements of the Open Compute Project Datacenter NVMe SSD specification 2.6. Although Kioxia lists PCIe 5.0 compliance, the drives operate at PCIe 4.0 x4 speeds of up to 16 GT/s per lane, which provides a theoretical maximum bandwidth of approximately 7.88 GB/s in each direction. While the company currently offers capacities of up to 30.72 TB, it has validated an architecture capable of supporting 122.88 TB drives, though it never revealed when such drives are set to be available, something not surprising in a world where 3D NAND memory is sold in advance.Interestingly, Kioxia did not disclose any actual performance characteristics of its LD4-series SSDs, including sequential read and write speeds, random read and write IOPS, or latency. The company also did not reveal their endurance ratings in drive writes per day (DWPD) or total bytes written (TBW), nor did it specify their power consumption. These characteristics are particularly important for hyperscale operators evaluating the cost, performance, and longevity of storage infrastructure.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: (Image credit: Kioxia)The key selling point of Kioxia's LD4-series and its E1.L form factor — 318.75 mm length × 38.4 mm height × 9.5 mm thick — is its ability to house numerous 3D NAND flash packages on an elongated printed circuit board, thus enabling multiple drives to be installed in a thin 1U server, offering vast capacities. This enables system manufacturers among those who build OCP-compliant servers to maximize storage capacity without increasing rack space requirements, which is particularly important for large-scale storage deployments.Kioxia is currently sampling 15.36 TB and 30.72 TB LD4 drives to select customers. The company has not disclosed when 122.88 TB configurations will become available or when the series will enter mass production. The drives will be demonstrated at the OCP Global Summit in San Jose in mid-October. items.author: Anton Shilov
items.titleZh: 铠侠推出面向超大规模数据中心的E1.L固态硬盘，容量高达122.88TB
items.descriptionZh:
铠侠（Kioxia）于周五发布了 LD4 系列固态硬盘（SSD），采用 E1.L 外形规格，容量最高可达 122.88TB，专为超大规模数据中心的高密度存储部署而设计。该系列基于成熟的 BiCS8 3D QLC NAND 闪存，主要面向 AI 数据仓库、对象存储等读取密集型工作负载。随着 AI 和对象存储场景对存储密度和容量需求不断攀升，超大规模运营商亟需在不增加机架空间的前提下扩展存储能力，LD4 系列正是针对这一背景推出。

在技术原理与创新方面，LD4 系列采用铠侠专有平台，符合 NVMe 2.0e 规范，采用单端口配置，并满足开放计算项目（OCP）数据中心 NVMe SSD 规范 2.6 的部分要求。尽管标称 PCIe 5.0 合规，但实际以 PCIe 4.0 x4 速度运行，每通道高达 16 GT/s，理论最大带宽约为 7.88 GB/s（每个方向）。其核心创新在于 E1.L 外形——长 318.75 mm、高 38.4 mm、厚 9.5 mm。这种细长的印刷电路板能够容纳大量 3D NAND 封装，从而在 1U 服务器中安装多个驱动器，提供巨大容量，同时不增加机架空间需求。对于构建 OCP 合规服务器的系统制造商而言，这有助于在不扩展机架空间的情况下最大化存储容量，对大规模存储部署尤为关键。

在性能参数与对比数据方面，铠侠目前提供 15.36 TB 和 30.72 TB 两种容量的 LD4 驱动器，并已验证其架构可支持 122.88TB 的驱动器，但尚未透露 122.88TB 配置的具体上市时间。值得注意的是，铠侠并未披露 LD4 系列的任何实际性能特征，包括顺序读写速度、随机读写 IOPS、延迟，也未公布耐久性评级（DWPD 或 TBW）以及功耗。这些参数对于超大规模运营商评估存储基础设施的成本、性能和寿命至关重要。因此，尽管容量指标亮眼，实际性能仍有待观察。

在技术影响与应用场景上，LD4 系列主要面向超大规模数据中心的高密度存储，如 AI 数据仓库和对象存储，可帮助系统制造商在不增加机架空间的情况下大幅提升存储容量。铠侠目前正向特定客户送样 15.36 TB 和 30.72 TB 的 LD4 驱动器，并将在 10 月中旬于圣何塞举行的 OCP 全球峰会上进行展示。不过，122.88TB 配置的可用时间以及该系列的量产时间均未公布。

背景是，特朗普长期支持AI。上个月，在业界围绕是否要“pacing”（控制节奏）前沿AI开发的讨论之后，他进入了亲机器人的“超速”状态。他现在的立场是：AI安全风险被夸大，美国公司需要加快开发，包括建设更多数据中心；他坚称数据中心会“非常受欢迎”，尽管民调数据相反。除了反对行业自我监管，他还决定用行政力量给AI改名。上个月，他在联合国讲话中宣称“artificial”这个词让智能显得虚假，并承诺把这项技术改名为“super intelligence”。上周，他签署行政令，禁止在可能的情况下使用“AI”。

改名行动迅速展开。美国AI标准与创新中心（CAISI，本身已是AI安全研究所的改名）又被改名为“超级智能推进创新与标准中心”（CAISSI）。司法部新闻稿也被修改，宣称一名在2017至2024年间向流媒体平台大量发布AI生成歌曲的男子犯下了“Super Intelligence-Assisted Music Streaming Fraud”。周四，特朗普宣布：“白宫认为，任何使用‘Artificial Intelligence’而不是更准确的新词‘Super Intelligence’的人，都是THE ENEMY！”

科技界一些大佬迅速跟进。特朗普的“第一伙伴”马斯克承诺把SpaceXAI改名为SpaceXSI；贝索斯表示喜欢这个说法，因为“artificial听起来不太好”；黄仁勋也采用了这个词——上个月特朗普曾在舞台上现场连线他，并声称“机器人不会接管”；Sam Altman也称赞这一命名，但表示OpenAI不会改名。

与此同时，特朗普正把“artificial”变成类似“hoax”“fake”的贬义词。他宣布不再使用长期偏好的“fake news media”，而是改称媒体为“artificial media”；在10月5日竞选集会上，他还称对战争推高物价的担忧“just artificial”。

但这场语言战并不容易赢。学界早已使用一个词的“superintelligence”，该词由Nick Bostrom在2014年同名书中普及，指的是可能超越人类思维的高度先进AI，而不是AI这个整体类别。它和AGI、“useful general intelligence”一样，是定义当前技术之后阶段的行业热词。特朗普强推“Super Intelligence”（两个词）会造成术语混乱。对Meta、微软等已押注超级智能的公司来说，这看似有利；在公众对AI反感上升时，一些公司也可能想要重塑品牌。但强制立即采用SI，会削弱企业把重大新AI产品宣传为“超级智能”的能力，因为这个标签会被套到从未来机器神到多年前音乐垃圾生成工具的一切东西上。中间多出的空格，还让这个领域显得掉价、土气。特朗普认真取的好名字，通常比不上他的贬称。

政治和法律上也有障碍。特朗普无法禁止国会使用“artificial intelligence”，这个词已出现在现有法律中，例如他标志性的《Take It Down Act》，行政机构在法庭上仍需引用。随着AI监管呼声增长，国会共和党人必须决定是否迎合特朗普，采用一个许多人觉得不直观、且背负其不受欢迎的亲产业、反监管立场的名字。更混乱的是，支持监管的参议员Bernie Sanders等人早已使用“superintelligence”的旧定义来推动限制强大AI，并在9月初共同提出《Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act》。

结论是，特朗普热爱命名，但他的语言胜利通常靠朗朗上口：简单绰号或独特搞笑的措辞。相比之下，“Super Intelligence”更像一种委婉语。许多美国人对AI产业有具体不满，尤其是数据中心；坚称这项技术“super”，并不能缓解这些担忧。若继续强推，反而会让他和AI行业显得虚弱。原文没有涉及具体技术原理、芯片性能或对比数据；其核心是AI命名、监管与产业政治。

history.title: Kioxia unveils E1.L SSDs for hyperscalers with up to 122.88TB capacity
history.description: Kioxia's LD4-series SSDs can store up to 122.88TB of data in a compact form-factor, but its performance remains a mystery.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Kioxia introduced its LD4-series solid-state drives (SSDs) in an E1.L form factor with capacities up to 122.88TB designed for high-density storage deployments in hyperscale data centers on Friday. The new drives use proven BiCS8 3D QLC NAND and are aimed at read-intensive workloads like AI data repositories and object storage, according to the manufacturer.Tom's Hardware Premium Roadmaps (Image credit: Future)Leading-edge foundry roadmapsNvidia Enterprise GPU and CPU roadmapAMD's Enterprise GPU and CPU roadmapIntel's roadmaps examined — 14A, Nova Lake, Diamond Rapids & AI accelerator pushCo-Packaged Optics (CPO) foundry roadmapsKioxia's LD4-series SSDs rely on the company's proprietary platform complying with the NVMe 2.0e specification and featuring a single-port configuration along with select requirements of the Open Compute Project Datacenter NVMe SSD specification 2.6. Although Kioxia lists PCIe 5.0 compliance, the drives operate at PCIe 4.0 x4 speeds of up to 16 GT/s per lane, which provides a theoretical maximum bandwidth of approximately 7.88 GB/s in each direction. While the company currently offers capacities of up to 30.72 TB, it has validated an architecture capable of supporting 122.88 TB drives, though it never revealed when such drives are set to be available, something not surprising in a world where 3D NAND memory is sold in advance.Interestingly, Kioxia did not disclose any actual performance characteristics of its LD4-series SSDs, including sequential read and write speeds, random read and write IOPS, or latency. The company also did not reveal their endurance ratings in drive writes per day (DWPD) or total bytes written (TBW), nor did it specify their power consumption. These characteristics are particularly important for hyperscale operators evaluating the cost, performance, and longevity of storage infrastructure.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: (Image credit: Kioxia)The key selling point of Kioxia's LD4-series and its E1.L form factor — 318.75 mm length × 38.4 mm height × 9.5 mm thick — is its ability to house numerous 3D NAND flash packages on an elongated printed circuit board, thus enabling multiple drives to be installed in a thin 1U server, offering vast capacities. This enables system manufacturers among those who build OCP-compliant servers to maximize storage capacity without increasing rack space requirements, which is particularly important for large-scale storage deployments.Kioxia is currently sampling 15.36 TB and 30.72 TB LD4 drives to select customers. The company has not disclosed when 122.88 TB configurations will become available or when the series will enter mass production. The drives will be demonstrated at the OCP Global Summit in San Jose in mid-October. history.author: Anton Shilov
history.titleZh: 铠侠推出面向超大规模数据中心的E1.L固态硬盘，容量高达122.88TB
history.descriptionZh:
铠侠（Kioxia）于周五发布了 LD4 系列固态硬盘（SSD），采用 E1.L 外形规格，容量最高可达 122.88TB，专为超大规模数据中心的高密度存储部署而设计。该系列基于成熟的 BiCS8 3D QLC NAND 闪存，主要面向 AI 数据仓库、对象存储等读取密集型工作负载。随着 AI 和对象存储场景对存储密度和容量需求不断攀升，超大规模运营商亟需在不增加机架空间的前提下扩展存储能力，LD4 系列正是针对这一背景推出。

在技术原理与创新方面，LD4 系列采用铠侠专有平台，符合 NVMe 2.0e 规范，采用单端口配置，并满足开放计算项目（OCP）数据中心 NVMe SSD 规范 2.6 的部分要求。尽管标称 PCIe 5.0 合规，但实际以 PCIe 4.0 x4 速度运行，每通道高达 16 GT/s，理论最大带宽约为 7.88 GB/s（每个方向）。其核心创新在于 E1.L 外形——长 318.75 mm、高 38.4 mm、厚 9.5 mm。这种细长的印刷电路板能够容纳大量 3D NAND 封装，从而在 1U 服务器中安装多个驱动器，提供巨大容量，同时不增加机架空间需求。对于构建 OCP 合规服务器的系统制造商而言，这有助于在不扩展机架空间的情况下最大化存储容量，对大规模存储部署尤为关键。

在性能参数与对比数据方面，铠侠目前提供 15.36 TB 和 30.72 TB 两种容量的 LD4 驱动器，并已验证其架构可支持 122.88TB 的驱动器，但尚未透露 122.88TB 配置的具体上市时间。值得注意的是，铠侠并未披露 LD4 系列的任何实际性能特征，包括顺序读写速度、随机读写 IOPS、延迟，也未公布耐久性评级（DWPD 或 TBW）以及功耗。这些参数对于超大规模运营商评估存储基础设施的成本、性能和寿命至关重要。因此，尽管容量指标亮眼，实际性能仍有待观察。

在技术影响与应用场景上，LD4 系列主要面向超大规模数据中心的高密度存储，如 AI 数据仓库和对象存储，可帮助系统制造商在不增加机架空间的情况下大幅提升存储容量。铠侠目前正向特定客户送样 15.36 TB 和 30.72 TB 的 LD4 驱动器，并将在 10 月中旬于圣何塞举行的 OCP 全球峰会上进行展示。不过，122.88TB 配置的可用时间以及该系列的量产时间均未公布。
